newsitem.title: USA: Liposome plummets on disappointing trial.
newsitem.headline: Liposome plummets on disappointing trial.

text.p: Liposome Co shares fell sharply Wednesday after the company said its lead product in development failed to demonstrate efficacy in Phase III clinical trials.
The study of the Ventus drug candidate for acute respiratory distress syndrome showed no difference in response between patients receiving the drug and those receiving a placebo.
Ventus had been widely hyped, and some analysts estimated that well over half of Liposome's market capitalization came from hopes that the product would be approved.
With 36 million shares outstanding, Liposome lost more than $570 million of its value Tuesday after releasing the disappointing news.

Sturza's Institutional Research analyst Evan Sturza said widespread expectations that Ventus would be approved by the Food and Drug Administration and enter the market next year helped make Liposome one of the 10 most highly capitalized companies in the biotech industry.
"Its list of recommendations read like a 'Who's Who on Wall Street,'" said Sturza, who had not recommended the stock.

Unlike many unsuccessful drug candidates that fail earlier in the trial process, Ventus made it all the way to Phase III trials without stirring serious concern among most investors who had bought the stock.
Mehta and Isaly analyst Sven Borho blamed a "sloppy analysis" of Phase II trials, which he said should have been seen as an early sign that the product did not work.
Borho also said investors were lured by the huge upside potential of Ventus. The drug would have been the only product on the market to treat acute respiratory distress syndrome.
Other sources said signs of Ventus's failure were recognized earlier by people familiar with the biotechnology industry, but Liposome managed to attract the interest of general investors.
The company frequently raised cash through public offerings. One investment group led by Dart Container Corp Chairman Kenneth Dart gradually build up a stake of over 20 percent.
Liposome's only product currently on the market is its Abelcet drug for systemic fungal infections.
